title: Model scoped claims and cited evidence relationships
summary: Build the relationship layer that lets a source support one claim while qualifying another. Preserve wording and locators, and prevent ingested assertions from changing established state without an assessment and authorized transition.
implementation: Define claim subjects, predicates, values, attribution, qualifiers, and temporal scope.
Implement multiple accepted relations targeting whole propositions or named components.
Accept explicit adapter locator-validation receipts, distinguishing exact passages from whole artifacts.
Append claim corrections and emit dependency changes without rewriting source wording.

acceptance.criterion: Support and qualification can coexist for one passage without losing scope.
acceptance.verification: Inspect mixed-relation fixtures and proposition components.

acceptance.criterion: Ingesting an assertion does not change matter state or merge identity.
acceptance.verification: Submit asserted approvals and equivalence claims; verify only claims appear.

acceptance.criterion: Unavailable or invalid citations are explicit.
acceptance.verification: Exercise missing bytes, absent quotation, reversed lines, and declared whole-artifact citations.

tests: A forecast does not establish the forecasted outcome.
Support for component A cannot prove component B.
Retraction does not prove the opposite proposition.
risks: Unscoped supporting labels can spread a narrow fact to an entire matter.

reuse.application: Adapt source-statement separation and exact-citation validation concepts without civic schemas.
